matched_rules.because: The datacenter control system was in the process of failing away from one of its control hosts, which is the exact 'when' condition for treating a control-system failover as a cooling-availability event.

The control system was unavailable, operators had minimum visibility into cooling health, and cooling did not transition to purge mode in part of the datacenter, matching the 'when' conditions for manually working the cooling chain and resetting PLCs.
Mechanical cooling is down in a portion of the datacenter and EC2 servers have begun shutting down due to overheating, indicating the thermal buffer is depleting and automated shutdowns have started.

next_actions.action: Manually investigate the affected cooling equipment, check the PLCs controlling the air handling units, reset affected equipment and PLCs into maximum cooling configuration, and confirm cooling is restored and temperatures are falling before standing down.

Treat the failover as a period of elevated risk to cooling availability, watch the cooling plant directly rather than only the control system, and verify that cooling systems have actually entered their designed maximum-cooling fallback.

Treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted; expect that once the buffer is gone, temperature will exceed safe operational thresholds and automated device shutdown will begin.

escalate.reason: Temperatures are rising and servers have begun powering off, which is the escalation trigger for R-004; additionally, control system failover is in progress and cooling has not transitioned to maximum cooling or purge mode in part of the datacenter.

not_covered: The specific cause of the control system failover (a bug in third-party control logic causing excessive interactions) is not addressed by any rule.
The failure of purge mode due to unresponsive PLCs is mentioned in guardrail G-003 but no rule provides a specific action for purge failure beyond manual PLC reset in R-004.
The fact that the control system failover mode that triggered this bug has been disabled in the interim (G-005) is not covered by any rule action.

per_finding.note: The triage explicitly lists the specific cause of the control system failover as not covered by any rule.
R-003 directs verifying cooling entered maximum-cooling fallback and R-004 covers manual cooling investigation, but neither names the partial-datacenter failure to transition.
R-004 directs checking and resetting PLCs, but the triage notes no rule provides a specific action for purge failure beyond manual PLC reset.
R-003 directs watching the cooling plant directly rather than only the control system, and R-004's conditions cite minimum visibility into cooling health.
R-004's next action is to manually investigate, reset affected equipment and PLCs, and put them into maximum cooling configuration.
The triage explicitly lists the interim disabling of the failover mode as not covered by any rule action.
No rule or action addresses training local operations teams to identify and remediate the situation.
No rule or action addresses modifying air handling unit control so purge mode bypasses PLC controllers.
The triage does not address recovery time or hardware retirement for affected instances and volumes.
